title: GRANT and REVOKE over schemas, tables, columns and rows

videos.script: Granting access to a table looks like one statement. {{grant}} It is the last of three. Before a role reaches a single row, it has to get into the database, then into the schema, and only then into the table. {{doors}} Each door has its own privilege and its own refusal. In this lesson you close all three, and open them one at a time for bruno, so you can read each refusal and know which door it came from. {{refusals}} Then you go smaller than a table. You hide one column from an analyst, and meet the column revoke that hides nothing. {{columns}} You switch on row-level security, and watch a table answer zero rows without a single error. {{rows}} You see what the public schema gives everybody, and what version 15 took away. And you finish with a layout for the whole database. One role owns everything and never logs in. One writes rows. One reads them. {{layout}} It is short enough to read in a minute. That is the point. Access you can read is access you can check. {{title}}
